chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid al-Khazzaz, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The dower of Fatima (peace be upon her) was a threadbare garment, a cracked shield, and her bed was a sheepskin; they would cast it down, spread it out, and sleep upon it.

key_terms.جَرْدَ بُرْدٍ: A simple, threadbare, or worn-out garment
key_terms.حُطَمِيَّةٍ: A shield that is slightly cracked or has minor defects
key_terms.حِبَرَةٍ: A type of shield, often described as cracked or slightly damaged
key_terms.دِرْعَ: A coat of mail or armor
key_terms.صَدَاقُ: Dower or bride price given in marriage

ai.seo_question: What was the dower of Fatima (peace be upon her) and what was her bed like?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the asceticism (zuhd) of Imam Ali and Fatima al-Zahra, emphasizing that their marital bond was founded on spiritual purity rather than material wealth. The specific mention of the sheepskin (*ihab kabsh*) as their sole bedding underscores the Prophet's household's deliberate rejection of worldly luxury, serving as a timeless model for Shia Muslims regarding simplicity in domestic life and the virtue of contentment.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed Al Khazzaz, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abu Maryam Al Ansary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The dower of Fatima<sup>asws</sup> was a threadbare garment, and a cracked shield, and her<sup>asws</sup> bed was of sheep skin which they<sup>asws</sup> would both cast (on the floor to sit upon), and as a bedspread, and they<sup>asws</sup> would sleep upon it’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn walid al-Khazzaz from Yunus ibn Ya’qub from abu Maryam al-Ansariy who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

mahr (dower) of Fatimah, ‘Alayha al-Salam, was from a gown which was patched, a shield of Hatmiyah and her bed was of hide of a ram which the wife and husband used as floor covering and bed on which they would sleep.’”
